name: dsu: repeat, self-union, then merge
why: 0-1 merges (2 comps, largest 2). 1-0 repeats, 2-2 is a self-union: no change. 1-2 joins vertex 2 to {0,1}: 1 comp, largest 3.

name: dsu: merging a big tree with a small one
why: {0,1}; {2,3}; {2,3,4} (largest 3); finally {0,1} joins {2,3,4}: 1 component of size 5.

name: dsu: no operations
why: The initial state is not reported, so no operations means an empty list.

name: kruskal: isolated vertices and a cycle
why: Triangle 0-1-2 drops its heaviest edge (id 0, weight 3). Cost 1+2=3. Vertices 3 and 4 are isolated, so 1+2=3 components.

name: kruskal: negative self-loop and parallel edges
why: The self-loop (-5) must never be chosen. Of the parallel 0-1 edges the cheaper one (id 2, weight -2) wins. Then 1-2 (id 3, weight 7). Cost -2+7=5.

name: kruskal: sum above 32 bits
why: Path graph: all three edges are forced. 3 * 10^9 = 3000000000 > 2^31.

name: kruskal: tied optima
why: Equilateral triangle: any 2 of 3 edges is optimal, cost 2. The checker accepts any such pair.

name: prim: isolated vertices and a cycle
why: Same graph as the Kruskal case, the optimum is unique.

name: prim: negative self-loop and parallel edges
why: Same reasoning as the Kruskal case.

name: prim: sum above 32 bits
why: Same reasoning as the Kruskal case.

name: prim: two separate components
why: Two independent edges, both forced, 5 + (-5) = 0. Prim must restart for the second component.

name: scc: two cycles joined by one edge
why: 0->1->2->0 is one SCC, 3->4->5->3 is another. The only cross edge is 2->3, so exactly one condensation edge.

name: scc: duplicates and a self-loop
why: No cycles except the self-loop, so every vertex is its own SCC. Duplicate 0->1 appears once in the condensation, the self-loop never.

name: topo: diamond (finished vertex reached twice is not a cycle)
why: Vertex 3 is reached from both 1 and 2. The second time it is already finished: no cycle. Order 0,1,2,3 (or 0,2,1,3) respects every edge.

name: topo: cycle in a part with no incoming edges from the rest
why: 2->3->4->2 is a directed cycle, so there is no valid order, although 0->1 alone would be fine.

name: dag: source in the middle, distance -1 is a real value
why: Vertex 0 can only reach 1, not the other way, so it is unreachable (null). 1->2 costs 3, 2->3 costs -4, so distance to 3 is -1 (a genuine cost, not 'unreachable').

name: dag: cycle not reachable from the source
why: 2<->3 is a cycle. The whole graph is checked, so the answer is 'not acyclic' even though the source cannot reach it.

name: dag: parallel edges and tied paths
why: To vertex 1 the cheaper parallel edge (id 1, weight 2) wins. To vertex 2: via 1 costs 2+1=3 (id 2), direct costs 3 (id 3). A tie, so parent_edge[2] may be 2 or 3.

name: dag: sum above 32 bits
why: A single path, distances are prefix sums.

name: dag: negative weights (README example)
why: 0->1->2 costs 3-7=-4, better than the direct 8. Then 2->3 gives 0. Vertex 4 has no incoming edge: null.
